evidence: AUTHORED FOR THIS PRODUCT. The brief at task/instruction.md is written in the voice of a recruiting team. It says the hard part is concurrency: 'nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts'. The rules note, hireops_rules.md sections 1-9, covers domain-specific mechanics: four roles (Recruiter, Hiring manager limited to Interview/Offer/Hired on their own jobs, Observer, Candidate); six stages with Rejected off to the side; reject-from-stage memory with reopen allowed only to that stage; a manual stage order shared by everyone; Interview places per job; versioned 409 stale-move refusal that names who made the change; optimistic moves with put-back and focus retained; all-or-nothing multi-card moves; single-level undo that is refused once any card is touched; activity lines; live updates within 15 seconds that keep typing, focus, the open card and scroll position; one staff-candidate conversation per application with 30-message paging and anchor retention; unread counted per person; seen marks where the Observer never counts; drafts held per person and per conversation that survive a sign-out and are hidden from another user on the same browser; and a candidate view with the wording table from section 7 and redaction of notes, reasons and board position. The seed follows the same domain: JOB-PLAT 'Platform Engineer' with interview_limit 3, APP-101 Noor Haddad, the candidate_status_labels map, thread_page_size 30, a 120-message long conversation and read markers. Both seed copies are byte-identical. All 39 functional criteria use the hro_ prefix and grade these product mechanics. For example, hro_seen (judge.toml:348-353) checks that opening by the Observer does not mark a message seen, and hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:131-138) checks focus on the card after a refused move. Polish (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume) and visual (hro_vis_*) are also written for this product. A grep of the frozen task found no foreign product names (Pellmoor, Threadline, Colderwater, TorqueBay, BazaarBridge, Docketlight, Boardloom, Ridgeline and others), no CHANGE_ME and no TODO. TEMPLATE CHECK: the task-authored prompts (tests/gates/*/prompt.md and tests/scored/*/prompt.md) all differ from the template. The template-controlled files tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the template, which is correct preservation and not a sign of cloning. NOT A NOUNS-SWAPPED SIBLING. (a) Pellmoor (projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline) is the closest sibling because it is also recruiting. It shares some generic pipeline invariants: no stage skipping (hiring-rules.md:3-5), capacity (lines 49-58) and atomic batch (lines 69-95). Its flows and criteria are different, though: interview panels and 1-5 scores, assessment-version freshness, vacancy openings reserved by offers, a reviewed batch-offer preview, actor-scoped durable retry receipts, a d3 funnel built from history, and a TypeScript/d3/esbuild stack. HireOps has none of panels, scores, assessments, receipts or funnel. Pellmoor has none of the manual in-stage order, undo, live non-disruptive updates, candidate conversations, unread or seen state, drafts, or the candidate portal. Even the shared ideas work differently: Interview places versus offer openings, and a multi-stage move to one target versus interview-to-offer batch only. Pellmoor also uses the retired reward.toml layout with a Codex judge. (b) Threadline (team chat) covers channels, threads, reactions, pins, mentions, webhooks and presence. HireOps conversations are 1:1 per application between staff and the candidate, with role-scoped participation, seen receipts and candidate redaction. Only generic chat mechanics overlap (load older messages without losing place, per-user unread), and the entities are not renamed copies. (c) TorqueBay, Boardloom and the other references are different domains. FITS THE SUITE'S DOMAIN PLAN. No repository document lists a formal domain plan. NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:201-203 asks for 'one coherent product, 2-3 connected workflows, roughly 3-5 key screens' and 'author distinct domain behavior'. HireOps has two connected workflows (pipeline board and conversations, linked through applications and the candidate portal) and four screens (Board, Conversations, Activity, candidate applications). task.toml:14-15 records provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task' and arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations', so the domain was supplied rather than self-selected to copy Pellmoor. The workspace has no other active HireOps-style live-collaboration recruiting task. COUNTEREXAMPLE ATTEMPTS. Clone test: I tried to turn Pellmoor into HireOps by renaming 'vacancy' to 'job' and 'openings' to 'interview places'. That fails, because more than half of HireOps' 39 functional criteria (the conversation, unread, seen, drafts, candidate, live-update, reorder and undo groups) have no counterpart in Pellmoor. A build that copied Pellmoor's behaviour would fail those criteria, so the rubric cannot be satisfied by a sibling's solution. The broken-app and conforming-alternative probes do not apply to this row because it judges distinctness, not grading. MINOR OBSERVATION (not a defect for this row): arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' leaves out the 'full-stack-node-express-sqlite-' stack prefix that most sibling task.toml files use (for example docketlight, coursemark, drawbill). This is a metadata convention point for the metadata rows, if any. It does not affect distinctness. No runtime evidence is needed to judge this row. This verdict does not claim any Oracle, model or portal result.
